messages:
maya: Quick proposal for Dedicated pools — trying to balance predictability for customers with overall utilization. TL;DR: ship a "soft quota + burst-smoothing" beta that enforces per-tenant reserved capacity but allows controlled spillover using proportional smoothing and budgeted burst credits. Seeking engineering feasibility + customer prioritization thoughts.

chris: This sounds promising. Can you sketch the behavior you expect when multiple tenants spike simultaneously?

maya: Sure. Desired behaviour: primary reserved cap never exceeded without using burst credits. Burst credits accrue at a rate tied to reserved size (e.g., 10% of steady capacity per hour). When spikes collide, we apply a proportional fairness algorithm: each tenant gets share of spare pool proportional to their reserved size and remaining burst credits. If spare pool is exhausted, preemption kicks in — newer requests get throttled first, with graceful fallback to lower-tier models.

sam: Implementation-wise, proportional fairness + credits is doable but we need clear SLO windows. We’ll need: 1) expressible policy config in API/console, 2) efficient admission controller that can evaluate shares in O(1) per request, and 3) metrics for credit burn rate.

jess: From CS: customers want simple primitives. "Soft quota" needs an obvious billing/alerting hook. Also major enterprise customers want guaranteed cold-start behavior if we preempt (they worry about sudden latency cliffs).

chris: Agree on expressible policy. I propose a config like: ```json
{
  "reserved_concurrency": 200,
  "burst_accrual_rate": 0.1,
  "burst_cap": 1.5,
  "spillover_policy": "proportional",
  "preempt_order": "most-recent-first",
  "graceful_fallback_model": "small-model-v2"
}
``` This gives us concrete knobs.

maya: Nice. For launch criteria the product team suggests: (a) stable admission controller for 2 weeks in staging under concurrent synthetic spikes, (b) integration tests for credit accounting (unit/integration), (c) docs + console UX for quota/credits, (d) 3 pilot customers signed and run for at least one week, (e) observability: per-tenant credit burn + 95/99 latency by route.

sam: Ops concerns: tracking credits per-tenant at scale — we should store credit state in a fast KV with bounded TTL and have an eventual-consistency fallback to avoid hard failures. That increases complexity. Also need an emergency global-throttle gate.

chris: Could we approximate credits using a token-bucket that we recompute per-minute and store only deltas? That avoids constant writes and keeps decision cheap at request time.

maya: That sounds like a viable implementation pattern. For the pilot cohort: jess, can you propose three customers (1 mid-market, 1 enterprise, 1 AI-native) who are okay with early beta? We want one that needs predictable latency and one that values cost smoothing.

jess: Yes — I'll reach out. Also request: surface estimated monthly cost delta if they use burst vs strict quota. Sales needs that to justify.

chris: Risk log: 1) unfairness under pathological spikes; 2) billing / invoicing confusion; 3) added operational complexity. Mitigations: canary rollout by org, rollback to strict quotas, and a 2-week pilot SLA.

maya: Scope negotiation: initial beta will exclude cross-region spillover and inter-tenant priority weights (keep weights proportional to reserved size only). Later phases can add explicit priority weights and region-aware routing.

sam: One more engineering ask — we need a deterministic simulation harness to test worst-case admission behavior. I can start a sim and share results next week.

maya: Great. Action items: chris -> proto config + token-bucket design by Thu; sam -> sim harness + storage options by Fri; jess -> pilot customers + cost mockups by EOW. I’ll draft product launch checklist and UX flows.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: staging admission-controller v0.1 ready? false; smoke-tests: pending.

chris: Noted. I’ll ping once the PR is ready for review. :thumbsup:

jess: On pilot outreach. Will post customer responses here.

maya: Thanks all. We’ll reconvene next Tue for go/no-go.
